reasons: The cited text (14.2) is a genuine critical deviation: Vendor takes exclusive ownership of Deliverables created specifically for Customer and leaves only a revocable, term-limited licence, squarely against the 'we own what we pay for' position.

The redline reaches the preferred position with an appropriate rewrite: it reverses the direction via an express irrevocable assignment of each Deliverable to Customer while expressly preserving Vendor Technology under 14.3 and the embedded-IP licence under 13.2, so no Customer IP/data is assigned to Vendor and no joint ownership is created.

The failed minimal-edit check is advisory only — reversing an ownership/assignment direction necessarily requires replacing the clause, and the edit stays scoped to 14.2 without touching unrelated obligations.

The comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (Vendor ownership of generic tools plus the perpetual, irrevocable 13.2 licence) while rejecting the revocable term-limited licence.

Cross-references are consistent with the finding's read of the document (14.1 Customer Data, 14.3 Vendor Technology, 13.2 perpetual licence), and the rule's Customer Data and no-joint-ownership elements are already satisfied, so no additional edits were needed.
